components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: Explore how Earth continuously recycles its water supply through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.

components.text: Heat from the sun warms water in oceans, lakes, and rivers, causing it to turn into invisible water vapor and rise into the atmosphere.
As water vapor rises, it cools and changes back into tiny liquid water droplets, gathering together to form clouds high in the sky.
When the water droplets in clouds become too heavy, gravity pulls them back down to Earth as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
Example: A puddle disappears on a sunny day due to evaporation. Quiz: 1. What turns liquid water into vapor? 2. How do clouds form? 3. What is rain considered?
